This petition is filed by the petitioner accused Nos. 123 under section 482 of Cr.P.C., for quashing the criminal proceedings in CC.No.475/2013 pending on the file of 37th ACMM, Bengaluru, arising out of Crime No.53/2009 and charge sheeted for the offence punishable under Sections 498(A) and 506 of IPC and Sections 3, 4 and 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. Heard the arguments of learner counsel for petitioner, learned HCGP for the State and learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
NC: 2024:KHC:2299 3.
The case of the petitioner is that on the complaint filed by respondent No.2, the police registered the FIR.

She has alleged in the complaint, that she was married to the petitioner No.1 in the year 2005, at the time of marriage, there was lot of dowry articles given, including cash which were given to the accused as dowry.
Once again after the marriage, they started demanding dowry and also site.
Even after begetting the female child, they are blaming her and demanded more money.
Hence, she was forced to approach the police for lodging the complaint.
The police investigated the matter and filed the charge sheet.

The learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the aged parents and they are from Tamil Nadu and they are not residing at Bangalore along with the complainant and accused No.1.

The problem started when the accused No.1 said to Vel Murugan vs State By Basavanagudi Women on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72980556/
2 have got job at Coimbatore, but the complainant was reluctant to go along with the accused and then the trouble started.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no specific allegation against the accused Nos.2 and 3 and they are aged persons and are unable to come to Bangalore for conducing/facing the trial.
Hence prayed for quashing criminal petition.

Per contra learned HCGP and learned counsel for respondent No.2 seriously objected the petition, that there is serious allegation against accused No.2 and 3 and specifically stated the harassment meted out by the complainant.
The complainant is the practicing advocate, in spite of that, they troubled her and after birth of female child trouble was more and demanded the site etc.
Hence, prayed for dismissing the petition.

5. Having heard the arguments and perusal of records, which reveals especially the complainant has given complaint almost about 5 pages in detail and she has narrated entire incident, including demand of dowry and the payment of dowry and further demand of gold, cash including the cell.
Though the petitioner counsel produced the documents, whether the petitioner No.1 already borrowed the loan and obtained the site and he is paying EMI, all these cannot be considered here.
It is matter of trial.
The petitioner can consider the same as defense in the trial court.
Merely the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are aged persons that itself is not a ground for quashing the criminal proceedings.
If at all any grievance, the petitioner can take the same as defense.

If at all they are not able to NC: 2024:KHC:2299 regularly attend court at Bangalore, they can seek exemption under Section 317 of Cr.P.C., as appearance may be dispensed by the Magistrate as there is no dispute in the identity of the accused persons.
Merely they are aged person and not able to come to the Bangalore for attending the cases, is not a ground for quashing the criminal proceedings.
Considering the same, I am of the view, the petition is devoid of merits and is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, this petition is dismissed.

The petitioner is granted liberty to file application for exemption and the Trial Court May consider the same and whenever necessary, the petitioner must be present for the purpose of framing of charge and recording the statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C., and final judgment.
